summary: Sokuo Eto (1888–1958) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his doctorate at Kyoto University in 1944. He founded Dokenryo in 1937 and became a professor at Komazawa University in 1953.

Solomon George FitzHerbert is a Tibetology and history scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford. He served as a Departmental Lecturer in Tibetan and Himalayan studies at Oxford and was a CNRS researcher as of 2019.

Soma Thera (1898–1960) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Benedict's College, Colombo, and under Jetavana Sayadaw in 1936. He was a member of the Servants of the Buddha around 1928 to 1936.

Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry, Columbia University, Wolfson College, and was a visiting scholar at Kyoto University in 2011.
Somboon Watana is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Panjab University in 1999 under the supervision of Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma.

Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara (1913–2013) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara. He was director of Mahamakut Buddhist University in 1961, abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (1961–2013), and Supreme Buddhist Patriarch of Thailand in 1989.
Somphong Santacitto is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat.

Sonam Chhoki is a Tibetology and history scholar who earned an MA at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a PhD at SOAS University of London. She worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Sonam Gyatso (born 1933) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko from around 1962 to 1974 and served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Sonam Kachru is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold. He has held fellowships at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science and Forum Transregionale Studien.

Sonam Kinga (born 1973) is a historian and Tibetologist who studied at Sherubtse College and Kyoto University. He worked as a researcher at the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from approximately 1999 to 2008.

Sonam Thakchoe is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania under Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, later holding an academic post there around 2003.

Sonam Tsering is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Gray Tuttle, as well as Khenzur Dawa, Drepung Khenzur Gyatso, Samdhong Rinpoche, Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Gyumé Khenzur Lobzang Trinlé.
Songeun Choe is a scholar of history and Buddhist studies who studied under Myung-dae Moon and earned a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Kiyohiko Munakata.

Sonja Arntzen (born 1945) is a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, as well as with Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

Sonja Glauch (born 1967) is a linguist who completed her degrees and habilitation at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg. She held positions at Erlangen-Nürnberg, Heidelberg University Library, the University of Vienna, and the University of Munich.

Sonya S. Lee is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Wu Hung. She taught at Swarthmore College and later held a post at the University of Southern California.

Soonil Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed an MA at Dongguk University and a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich. He held an editorial post at Dongguk University.

Sophus Bugge (1833–1907) was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1858. He held a post at Uppsala University and served as professor of comparative philology, Indo-European linguistics, and Old Norse at the University of Oslo from 1866.

Soshuku Shibatani (born 1954) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and earned master's and doctoral degrees at Koyasan University. He has held positions at Sonoda Women's University, Koyasan University, and Junrei Henro Kenkyukai.
